name: NJ-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Herb Conaway holds a D+5 district with a roughly twelve-to-one fundraising edge
Republican Michael McGuire's campaign is nearly broke, with about $800 on hand
Fundamentals point to a favorable 2026 national environment for Democrats
No public polls or expert ratings; prediction markets price Conaway near 94%
model.rationale: Conaway pairs incumbency in a Democratic-leaning district with a lopsided money advantage, while McGuire has raised under $80,000 and lacks outside support; district fundamentals and prediction markets both point to a comfortable Democratic win.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending for McGuire or a sharper-than-expected national shift toward Republicans could narrow what is otherwise a lopsided contest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Herb Conaway, a Democratic incumbent first elected in 2024, seeks a second term in a New Jersey district that leans Democratic by about five points. He enters the general election with a decisive financial advantage, having raised roughly $935,000 and holding about $439,000, while Republican Michael McGuire has raised under $80,000 and reported only about $800 on hand. Two minor-party candidates, an independent and a Green, are also on the ballot but show no visible funding.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbent's resources, and a national environment expected to favor Democrats in 2026. Prediction markets put Conaway's chances around 94 percent. The combination of incumbency, a friendly district, and a lopsided money gap makes Conaway a clear favorite, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty.
